salesLanguage.headline: EX-70-H2X: gets the signal from one place to another without moving the equipment
salesLanguage.plainEnglishSummary: Use this when the source, display, USB device or control point is too far away for a simple local cable.
salesLanguage.customerValue: It lets the room be built around where people and displays need to be, rather than where short cables happen to reach.
salesLanguage.realWorldApplication: Displays away from the rack, lecterns, teaching rooms, meeting rooms and point-to-point signal paths.
salesLanguage.salespersonCue: Start with distance and what has to travel: video only, video plus USB, audio, control or network.
talkTrack: It solves a distance problem.
Use it when the video path needs reliable point-to-point extension.
It is usually simpler than AV-over-IP when the path is one source to one display.
discoveryPrompts: How far is the source from the display or USB device?
What signals need to travel over the same path?
Is this a single fixed route or does it need to switch between many destinations?
avoidPositioningAs: Do not use an extender as a routing system when many sources and many displays need flexible switching.
marketApplications: Long-distance video, USB, control and network transport

consultant.headline: EX-70-H2X: architecture fit and trade-off view
consultant.pitch: Use this view to decide whether the project is simply a defined distance problem or whether routing, switching or networked AV is actually required.
consultant.value: Helps separate a technically possible product choice from the strongest design choice for the application, budget, risk and future expansion.
talkTrack: Validate the application first, then decide whether this product family is the cleanest architecture.
Compare against simpler or more scalable alternatives where the requirement is fixed, expandable, distance-led or conferencing-led.
Use the specification as evidence after the room workflow and signal architecture are clear.

positioningNotes: Use for architectural judgement, product-family selection and proposal-safe trade-off language.

avoidPositioningAs: Do not let a feature match override the real application, architecture or operational requirement.

featureLines: WyreStorm provides solutions for today’s demanding LECTURING spaces.

Extending 4K UHD content at 4:4:4/60 up to 70m/230ft, the EX-70-H2X is compatible with the latest HDR standards including HDR-10 and HLG up to 60Hz; Dolby Vision is supported at 30Hz. Powerful Class A HDBaseT transmission means Ethernet, IR & RS-232 are also supported, with the addition of 2-way PoH for flexible installation options. The HDMI loop-output means that source content can be sent to multiple locations by simply cascading the signal to additional extenders or switchers.

Knowing the speed at which technology moves, at WyreStorm we're always looking ahead. That's why we've included our VLC chipset (Variable Lossless Compression) in this extender meaning seamless support of the next shift in content technology: 4K/60 HDR-10 & HLG and even up to 4:4:4.

HDR Content has recently enjoyed an up-shift in refresh rates after starting its life at 24Hz on UHD Blu-Ray discs. High frame-rate HDR is now available at 60Hz on certain discs and via gaming consoles like the Xbox One X. The EX-70-H2X is now ready to support both HDR-10, HLG at 60Hz and Dolby Vision content up to 30Hz.

Proudly flying the flag for the full Class A HDBaseT TM feature set, the EX-70-H2X levels-up.?Supporting not only HDR video, HD Audio and control, but also allowing Ethernet pass-through and 2-way PoH.?This allows the?extender to?be powered from a single PSU, located at either end.

The source loop-output on the transmitter allows a multitude of system expansion options without the need for an external splitter. The signal can be cascaded to a second or third extender to feed extra screens, to a matrix switcher so it can be made part of a larger system or even sent to a NetworkHD encoder forming a hybrid distribution system.
Compatible with the latest HDR standards, including HDR-10+, HLG content, with support for Dolby Vision TM up to 30Hz ?C Supports all VESA resolutions within the HDMI 2.0 specification
2-way PoH (Power over HDBaseT) enables either transmitter or receiver to be remotely powered by the other unit
2ch PCM audio and multichannel HD audio supports 7.1, DTS-X and Dolby Atmos TM
Note:? Serial control via RS-232 only supported when connected to a compatible HDBaseT transmission device with routable RS-232
Threaded bushings allow use of both standard and locking 18v DC power plugs
Supported file types: jpg, jpeg, png, txt, pdf, doc, docx
